- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above recent peak unless sentiment drops.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model tends to lag in correcting downward trends; if 3+ consecutive days of falling prices, forecast should be adjusted downward by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts early in the window; reduce first 5–7 forecast values by 1–2% to align with true mean reversion.
- If sentiment is high but price is falling, model may misread sentiment as bullish; check for divergence between sentiment and price trend; if mismatch, reduce forecast by 1–3%.
